fields.Front: Slide 47 (1 Gb/s link, users 100 Mb/s when active, active 10%): write the exact expression for the probability quoted on the slide for 35 users.
fields.Back:
P(more than 10 active) = Σr=11..35 C(35, r) (0.1)r (0.9)35−r ≈ 0.000424 (≈ 0.0004).
Source: the OWL handout binomial distribution – for circuit switch problem.pdf.

fields.Front: Why does the slide-47 sum start at r = 11 and not r = 10?
fields.Back: The link carries 1 Gb/s = 10 users × 100 Mb/s. Exactly 10 active users fit, so the link is only overloaded when more than 10 (11 or more) are active at once.

fields.Text: Binomial probability of exactly r successes in n trials: P(r) = {{c1::C(n, r) p<sup>r</sup> (1 − p)<sup>n−r</sup>}}, where C(n, r) = {{c1::n! / (r! (n − r)!)}}. In the slide-47 problem n = {{c1::35}}, p = {{c1::0.1}}.

fields.Front: Slide 47 says P(>10 of 35 active) is "less than .0004". What is the exact value, and how should you treat an option reading "≈ 0.0004"?
fields.Back: Exact: 0.000424, slightly MORE than 0.0004, so the slide's "less than" is loose. The handout gives ≈ 0.000424 and the textbook says ≈ 0.0004. Treat "≈ 0.0004" or "0.000424" as correct.

fields.Front: Quick calculator check for slide 47: which single term dominates the sum, and what is it worth?
fields.Back: r = 11: C(35,11)(0.1)<sup>11</sup>(0.9)<sup>24</sup> ≈ 3.3 × 10<sup>−4</sup>, about 78% of the total. Terms r = 11–13 give over 99%. So the answer is "a few × 10<sup>−4</sup>", i.e. ≈ 0.0004.

fields.Front: Slide 47 asks "what happens if > 35 users?" Answer with numbers.
fields.Back: P(more than 10 active) climbs steeply: 35 → 0.0004, 40 → 0.0015, 50 → 0.009, 60 → 0.034, 70 → 0.087. More users means more frequent overload, so queueing delay, buffer overflow and packet loss become likely. That is why packet switching needs congestion control.

fields.Front: Slide 47: what are the complement form of the probability and the expected number of active users, and why does the expected value explain packet switching's win?
fields.Back: 1 − Σr=0..10 C(35,r)(0.1)r(0.9)35−r = 1 − 0.999576 = 0.000424. Expected active = n·p = 35 × 0.1 = 3.5, far below the 10 the link can carry, so statistical sharing rarely overloads it.

fields.Front: Generalize: a 10 Mb/s link, users need 500 kb/s when active and are active 10% of the time. What is the circuit-switching capacity, and what is the packet-switching overload event?
fields.Back: Circuit: 10 Mb/s ÷ 500 kb/s = 20 users. Packet switching overloads when more than 20 are active: Σr=21..n C(n,r)(0.1)r(0.9)n−r.
